title: Alternative Care Arrangements when Childcare Centres Close Due to Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease
what_it_is: Alternative Care Arrangements when Childcare Centres Close Due to Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease

sections.label: HFMD prevention in preschools
sections.summary: Preventive measures are in place to minimise HFMD transmission in preschools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Preventive measures are in place to minimise the transmission of HFMD in preschools.

sections.label: Centre closures over three years
sections.summary: Over the past three years, there have not been more than five centre closures every year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Over the past three years, there have not been more than five centre closures every year.

sections.label: Childcare leave for working parents
sections.summary: Each working parent with children below seven has six days of childcare leave yearly, or 12 days per couple.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Each working parent with children below the age of seven has six days of childcare leave per year, or a total of 12 days of childcare leave for every couple.

sections.label: Firms offering ad hoc flexible work
sections.summary: The proportion of firms providing ad hoc flexible work arrangements rose from 70% in 2015 to 77% in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: The proportion of firms providing ad hoc flexible work arrangements rose from 70% in 2015 to over three-quarters at 77% in 2016.

sections.label: Childcare options and ECDA remit
sections.summary: Parents are encouraged to explore other caregivers, and providing such services is beyond ECDA's remit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Apart from taking leave and arranging for flexible work to care for the children, we do encourage parents to explore grandparents, relatives, friends, domestic helpers, fellow parents to pool together efforts to care for the children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: However, we do seek their understanding that this is a necessary step to break the cycle of transmission of the disease to other children and other families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: But more directly to the Member's question on whether we plan to provide such services, I think that is beyond the remit of ECDA to do so.

sections.label: Companies taking expansive flexible work approach
sections.summary: A key measure is for companies to take a much more expansive approach to flexible work arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: One of the key measures we mentioned is for companies to take a much more expansive approach in terms of their flexible work arrangements, and we are encouraged that that will continue to develop.

sections.label: ECDA care services for sick children
sections.summary: The speaker says ECDA cannot provide care services for children affected by HFMD or other illnesses, despite parental inconvenience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: But in terms of taking a very specific step for ECDA to provide for such care services, I would suggest that the Member's question is with regard to students affected by HFMD, but there are also other illnesses that children contract from time to time, and parents do sometimes face inconvenience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: I do not think it is possible for ECDA to provide that service.
